title: Consensus-driven change safety: atomic snapshots + preflight apply simulator
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Implement a consensus-driven safety layer for config applies that combines atomic snapshots, a preflight apply simulator (traffic replay in sandbox), and multi-signal gating. The goal is to detect cost/latency regressions or functional divergences before a live apply and to enable an automated, safe reconciliation path when inconsistencies are detected. This ticket covers design, prototype, and a limited canary rollout of the apply-simulator + snapshot reconciliation pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Create an atomic snapshot format for runtime configuration and transient serving state (KV cache markers, sharding hints) that can be atomically recorded and restored in the sandbox.

Build a preflight apply simulator that replays mirrored traffic against a sandboxed runtime using the snapshot and emits the same telemetry signals as production (latency, error rates, token-per-request cost, cache hit ratio).
Implement a consensus evaluator that ingests signals (latency delta, cost delta, error rate delta, cache health) and produces a binary pass/fail verdict along with confidence score.
If the consensus evaluator fails, abort the live apply and produce a reconcile plan that includes the snapshot id, diff, and a suggested corrective change or rollback action.
Run a 1% traffic canary using the new system for two weeks with automatic abort on fail and no customer-facing regressions observed in the canary cohort.
Document the end-to-end runbook and expose per-apply decision traces in Console's rollout UI.
Security review completed and KMS keys used for snapshot metadata are audited.
implementation_notes: Components: snapshot-store (S3 + manifest), preflight-sim (mirror runner + sandboxed runtime), consensus-evaluator (weighted rule engine), reconcile-runner (state diff applier)
Snapshot must be content-addressed and immutable; include minimal transient state (KV cache checksums, routing hints) to keep size bounded.
Telemetry hooks: ensure preflight emits the same event schema as production to reuse dashboards and alerting rules.
Consensus policy initially: 60% weight latency/cost, 30% weight error/functional checks, 10% weight cache-health heuristics. Policy should be configurable via Console.
Simulator must support token-limited replay and synthetic amplification for low-traffic routes to hit tail latency numbers.
Integrate with existing change audit log and link each snapshot/decision to a GitHub PR and Linear key.
Rollbacks are represented as a plan object with snapshot id + ordered steps; reconcile-runner must be idempotent and report final state hashes.
Plan for eventual ML-based signal fusion in a follow-up (separate ticket).
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal dev/staging only, verify snapshot/restore and simulator fidelity (2 weeks). Phase 2: limited canary (1% traffic) with 72-hour ramp window and automatic abort on consensus fail (4 weeks). Phase 3: 10% canary with manual signoff and metrics review (2 weeks). Phase 4: global enable behind feature flag with monitoring and 24/7 on-call observation (2 weeks).
qa_steps: Create a synthetic workload for low-latency and high-throughput routes and mirror 1k requests per minute into simulator; verify metrics match within tolerance.
Introduce a config that intentionally degrades batching policy; confirm consensus-evaluator flags fail and aborts apply.
Test snapshot restore followed by reconcile-runner to ensure state hashes match pre-snapshot when applied in sandbox.
Simulate partial failure (simulator node crash) and confirm automatic fallback: mark preflight inconclusive and require manual signoff.
Run security validation: verify snapshots are encrypted and metadata ACLs restrict access to ops team.

2025-01-28 Mikael Hansen (Review): Concern about false positives from cache-health heuristic. Suggested adding decay window and comparing warmed vs cold cache baselines.
2025-02-03 PM review (Ava Chen): Product asks for an operator override to force-apply with audit trail; accepts for P1 rollout with explicit warning in Console.

2025-02-07 Ops (Priya Nair): Incident learnings referenced INC-2025-01 where a rapid batch-size shrink caused a 30% throughput loss. We will include a simulated batch-size-regression scenario in preflight.
2025-02-10 Daniel Kim: Implemented consensus-evaluator v0 (rule engine). Tests show it catches simulated 18% P95 latency regressions in staging. Next: tie to abort path and UI traces.
notes_for_reviews: Please focus review on snapshot manifest size and which transient state to include — trade-off between fidelity and snapshot storage cost.
Security reviewers: confirm KMS usage for snapshot metadata and that snapshots are not containing customer PII.
SRE: verify the abort path is fast (sub-10s) and does not leave partial traffic routing state.
